evidence: src/domain/errors.ts: `class DomainError` with code union 'not_found' | 'invalid_input' | 'insufficient_stock' | 'invalid_transition' is the shared error abstraction
src/domain/order.ts: `nextState` and `assertCancellable` throw `new DomainError("invalid_transition", ...)`, consistent with errors.ts
src/domain/order.ts: `ORDER_STATES` is the single source for `OrderState`, `isOrderStatus`, and `nextState`
src/domain/product.ts: `availableOf` is the single availability calculation, used by both `reserve` and `toStockLevel`
src/domain/product.ts: `reserve` throws `new DomainError("insufficient_stock", ...)`, consistent with errors.ts
src/domain/order.ts: `assertCancellable` lists 'placed'/'paid'/'packed' by name instead of deriving them from ORDER_STATES. This is minor and not duplicated anywhere else.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All three files cover one concern: the order-fulfilment domain model. errors.ts defines the single DomainError type with a closed set of codes. order.ts and product.ts both use it for every rule violation instead of throwing raw errors or creating their own error types. order.ts keeps the order lifecycle in one place: ORDER_STATES is the only source of the state sequence, and isOrderStatus and nextState are both derived from it. product.ts keeps the stock invariant in one place: availableOf (onHand - reserved) is the only place availability is calculated, and both reserve and toStockLevel call it rather than recomputing it. I found no unrelated concerns, no rule duplicated across files, and nothing that bypasses the module's own abstractions. One minor point: assertCancellable lists 'placed' | 'paid' | 'packed' by name instead of deriving the cancellable states from their position in ORDER_STATES. That would drift if the state list changed. Still, it is the only home of the cancellation rule, so it is not duplicated and does not reach the level of a violation.
